claims.text: A method combining ab initio phonon calculations with machine-learning descriptors of mass variance and local lattice distortion can accurately rank HEA compositions by phonon thermal conductivity.
The predictive method can identify HEAs with exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity for thermal-insulation applications.
The candidate library consists of single-phase equiatomic HEAs with uniform solid-solution microstructures.
The screening approach uses first-principles phonon dispersions and machine-learned descriptors representing mass disorder and local lattice strain.
Candidate HEAs will be processed under identical and strictly controlled cooling and homogenization conditions.
Thermal-conductivity measurements will be performed at room temperature in an inert atmosphere.
Atomic-scale chemical disorder induces mass fluctuations and local lattice distortions.
Mass fluctuations and local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering.
Increased mass contrast and local lattice strain disrupt coherent phonon propagation in HEAs.
Disruption of coherent phonon propagation reduces phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
The combined computational method captures phonon-scattering mechanisms more accurately than conventional mixing rules.
HEAs identified as low-kappa by the method will have at least 20% lower phonon thermal conductivity than a control baseline selected using traditional averaging methods.
The claimed applicability is limited to single-phase, fully disordered HEAs without secondary-phase formation.
Ordering, precipitation, or significant extrinsic defects may invalidate the predictions.
Prior experimental calibration of the combined predictive descriptors is limited.
Unaccounted extrinsic phonon-scattering effects may alter the magnitude of the predicted thermal-conductivity reduction.
The benchmark compares HEAs predicted to have low thermal conductivity against a control group predicted to have average thermal conductivity, with both groups synthesized under identical conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if fewer than 60% of predicted low-kappa HEAs exhibit at least 20% lower thermal conductivity than the control-group baseline.
